proposal.name: cryptography
proposal.note: Measures solana-bn254 (syscall/solana-bn254), the crate behind Solana's alt_bn128 and Poseidon syscalls. It is a no_std crate with no runtime dependencies, so every instruction counted is its own code. On arm64 it runs the portable backend, because the x86-only paths are excluded at compile time. There are three cachegrind instruction-count metrics, all seeded: chained Poseidon hashes across the syscall widths, G1 scalar multiplication with additions and encoding round trips, and pairings, a 4-pair multi-pairing and a product-is-one check shaped like Groth16 verification. In calibration all three were deterministic (cv 0) and only 0.2 to 0.5% of each count was not the library's work. All 243 tests are stable. The equivalence harness covers every Poseidon width, including the wrong-length and unreduced inputs, G1/G2 decoding of valid, flagged and garbage bytes, edge scalars, and pairing and Gt operations. Patches may only touch src/, and the in-file test modules are protected.
